concerns: The manuscript provides no controlled, converged, parameter-matched classical baseline or component ablation, so the utility of the quantum-inspired periodic encoding and gated mixing over a standard vision transformer is unestablished.

The simulator diagnostic uses one-epoch, non-converged runs with unmatched parameter counts, and the authors state the accuracy differences are optimization snapshots rather than evidence of architectural superiority.

The multi-dataset and ImageNet results are single-run point estimates without repeated seeds or uncertainty intervals, and the ImageNet comparisons are explicitly heterogeneous external literature values rather than controlled pairwise evidence.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The mathematical characterization and conceptual delineation of the method are clear, and the authors scrupulously disclaim quantum advantage and overclaims. However, under library curation standards, scientific promotion requires substantiated empirical evidence of the architectural contribution's value, which is precluded here by the total absence of converged, controlled classical baselines and ablations.

inspired Transformer for vision tasks with three compo-
nents: (i) angle-inspired encoding that maps image tokens
to learned trigonometric Hilbert-space features analogous

visual recognition.

evidence.excerpt:
motivated by
multiplicative terms in a variational quantum circuit (VQC).
It does not instantiate or simulate physical entanglement.
For image tokens X∈R B×N×D and labels y, QiT
solves standard supervised classification by minimizing
cross-entropy for fΘ(X). The design reverses the usual
hybrid construction: rather than executing classical atten-
tion through quantum circuits, it isolates selected quantum-
motivated functional forms and evaluates them with conven-
tional GPU kernels. QiT consequently preserves parallel to-
ken processing, standard backpropagation, and the O(N 2D)
attention complexity of a Vision Transformer while avoid-
ing circuit simulation, repeated measurement, and quantum-
hardware constraints. The resulting model enables these
inductive biases to be evaluated on vision benchmarks at a
scale that is currently impractical for circuit-based attention.
Contributions.

rate decay, random cropping, horizontal flipping, and color
jitter on four Tesla T4 GPUs; per-GPU batch sizes appear in
Table 5. For Q3, the QiT-XS/S/B variants use the parameter
and FLOP budgets reported in Table 4. Results must be
interpreted within each protocol rather than compared across

Reporting scope.All tables report point estimates from
the available runs. The current records do not include re-
peated seeds, uncertainty intervals, complete optimizer hy-
perparameters, reduced-class CIFAR split definitions, or the
energy-measurement procedure. We therefore use the results
to document observed accuracy, runtime, and scalability,
not statistical superiority. A final reproducible submission
should provide these missing details and repeated-run confi-
dence intervals.

compute from 3.8 to 5.6 GFLOPs. Scaling from S to B
adds 14.7M parameters and 5.9 GFLOPs for a further 0.9
percentage-point gain, reaching 78.3%. This monotonic
but diminishing gain indicates that the architecture remains
trainable as capacity grows, although it does not establish
optimal scaling.

ResNet-50 accuracy and exceeds the listed ViT-B/16 re-

are not controlled comparisons because input resolution,
augmentation, optimization, and pretraining may differ. QiT
trails DeiT-B by 3.5 points and the strongest spectral and
state-space entries by 3.8–5.4 points. Accordingly, Table 4
supports ImageNet-scale

blocking_reasons: The manuscript provides no controlled, converged, parameter-matched classical baseline or component ablation, so the utility of the quantum-inspired periodic encoding and gated mixing over a standard vision transformer is unestablished.

The simulator diagnostic uses one-epoch, non-converged runs with unmatched parameter counts, and the authors state the accuracy differences are optimization snapshots rather than evidence of architectural superiority.

The multi-dataset and ImageNet results are single-run point estimates without repeated seeds or uncertainty intervals, and the ImageNet comparisons are explicitly heterogeneous external literature values rather than controlled pairwise evidence.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard supervised classification setup using canonical datasets without evaluator reuse.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Top-1 classification accuracy and runtime/FLOP metrics on standard benchmark test sets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard cross-entropy loss minimized via backpropagation with AdamW during training.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: While the manuscript is remarkably frank and explicitly caveats its empirical limitations, the available evidence fails to demonstrate whether the proposed quantum-inspired inductive biases provide any actual utility or benefit over standard, matched vision transformers.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation lacks controlled, matched classical baselines and component ablations; the simulator comparison evaluates an unconverged one-epoch run with unmatched parameters, the multi-dataset benchmark provides no baseline comparison, and ImageNet results merely tabulate heterogeneous external literature numbers.

evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard cross-entropy loss minimized via backpropagation with AdamW during training.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly note that runs are single-seed point estimates without error intervals, component ablations are absent, classical baselines in the diagnostic did not converge, and hyperparameter/energy details are omitted.
primary.method_assessment: The architecture is well-specified, mapping tokens through learned bounded trigonometric features prior to self-attention projections alongside a gated MLP block, with clear proofs that unprojected similarities form a cosine kernel while projected attention remains bilinear.
primary.quality_rationale: The mathematical characterization and conceptual delineation of the method are clear, and the authors scrupulously disclaim quantum advantage and overclaims. However, under library curation standards, scientific promotion requires substantiated empirical evidence of the architectural contribution's value, which is precluded here by the total absence of converged, controlled classical baselines and ablations.
primary.scoped_contribution: QiT translates quantum-inspired motifs—angle-based periodic feature encoding and gated multiplicative channel mixing—into fully classical differentiable tensor operations for vision transformers without claiming quantum advantage.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The mathematical characterization and conceptual delineation of the method are clear, and the authors scrupulously disclaim quantum advantage and overclaims. However, under library curation standards, scientific promotion requires substantiated empirical evidence of the architectural contribution's value, which is precluded here by the total absence of converged, controlled classical baselines and ablations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly note that runs are single-seed point estimates without error intervals, component ablations are absent, classical baselines in the diagnostic did not converge, and hyperparameter/energy details are omitted.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
